Rashi on Ketubot 28b:10:1.english: At the ketzatza - Later [the Gemara] explains it.

Rashi on Ketubot 28b:10:2.english: Of the daughter of so-and-so to so-and-so - When so-and-so married the daughter of so-and-so.

Rashi on Ketubot 28b:10:3.hebrew: ושהיינו מוליכין כו' על ידי עצמו - אם כך העיד התינוק: "על ידי היה אבא שולח לו חלה ומתנות":
Rashi on Ketubot 28b:10:3.english: And that we would bring, etc., by himself - If the child testified thus: "Through me, [my] father would send him challah and [priestly] gifts."

Rashi on Ketubot 28b:10:4.hebrew: אם היה עובד כוכבים ונתגייר - והעיד משנתגייר שראה את אלה בנכריותו, אינו נאמן:
Rashi on Ketubot 28b:10:4.english: If he was an idolater and converted - and he testified after he converted that he saw these [things] in his gentile state, he is not deemed credible.

Rashi on Ketubot 28b:13:1.english: A sample - A sign and a token of remembrance for future generations.

Rashi on Ketubot 28b:1:1.english: Steward - [His master] entrusted his property into his hand to bring in and take out for commerce.

Rashi on Ketubot 28b:1:2.hebrew: הרי זה לא יצא לחירות - ולא אמרינן אי לאו דשחרריה, לא הוה יזיף מיניה ולא הוה שביק ליה לנהוג מנהג בן חורין. ושמעינן מינה דיש עבד שלומד תורה:
Rashi on Ketubot 28b:1:2.english: This one has not gone out to freedom - And we do not say [that] had he not emancipated him, he would not have borrowed from him and would not have allowed him to conduct himself in the manner of a free man. And we learn from this that there is a slave who studies Torah.

Rashi on Ketubot 28b:2:1.hebrew: בתרומה דרבנן - כגון תרומת חוצה לארץ או פירות, המנינהו להני להאכילו על פיהם:
Rashi on Ketubot 28b:2:1.english: Of rabbinic terumah - For example, terumah of outside the Land [of Israel] or [of] fruits — [the Sages] trusted these [witnesses] to feed him [it] on their word.

Rashi on Ketubot 28b:2:2.hebrew: הכי גרסינן דתניא שאין חולקין תרומה לעבד כו' - ורישא דברייתא: כהנת שנתערב וולדה בוולד שפחתה, שניהן יוצאין לגורן ונוטלין חלק אחד, שאין חולקין תרומה לעבד כו'. הלכך, אי אזיל חד מינייהו לא פלגינן ליה, דלמא אתי לאחזוקי בכהן, ודלמא האי ניהו העבד:
Rashi on Ketubot 28b:2:2.english: This is how we read [the text]: As it is taught [in a baraita], "One does not distribute teruma to a slave, etc." - And the beginning of the baraita [is]: A priest's wife whose child was intermingled with the child of her maidservant — both of them go out to the threshing floor and take one portion [together], for one does not distribute teruma to a slave, etc. Therefore, if one of them goes [alone], we do not distribute [teruma] to him, lest he come to be presumed a priest, when perhaps this one is the slave.

Rashi on Ketubot 28b:3:1.hebrew: במקומו של ר' יהודה - משום הכי אמר אין חולקין:
Rashi on Ketubot 28b:3:1.english: In the place of Rabbi Yehuda - Because of this, he said, "They do not distribute [teruma]."

Rashi on Ketubot 28b:4:1.english: The animals of the righteous - [This refers to] the donkey of Rabbi Pinchas ben Yair, in [the chapter] Hakol Shochatin (Chullin 7a).

Rashi on Ketubot 28b:5:1.english: He saw in the place of Rabbi Yosei - [He saw] that they apportioned terumah to him at the threshing floor.

Rashi on Ketubot 28b:5:2.english: And he testified in the place of Rabbi Yehuda - And there they did not distribute terumah to the slaves of priests.

Rashi on Ketubot 28b:6:1.hebrew: בית הפרס - החורש את הקבר הרי זה עושה בית הפרס מאה אמה, שכך שיערו שהמחרישה מולכת את עצמות המת. ודלמא נגע או הסיט המהלך בו את עצם כשעורה, שמטמא במגע ובמשא:
Rashi on Ketubot 28b:6:1.english: Beit haperas - One who plows over a grave thereby creates a beit haperas [an area of] one hundred cubits, for so did [the Sages] estimate that the plow carries the bones of the corpse; and perhaps one who walks in it touched or moved a bone [the size] of a barleycorn, which conveys impurity through contact and through carrying.

Rashi on Ketubot 28b:6:2.hebrew: מנפח אדם בית הפרס - וסומך על כך, שאם יש עצם רואהו. ואע"ג דמאהיל, לא חיישינן, דאין עצם כשעורה מטמא באהל עד דאיכא שדרה או גולגולת שלמה או רוב בנין או רוב מנין:
Rashi on Ketubot 28b:6:2.english: A person may blow [on] a beit haperas - and rely on this, that if there is a bone, he sees it. And even though he overshadows [it], we are not concerned, for a bone the size of a barleycorn does not convey impurity via a tent unless there is a spine, or a complete skull, or the majority of [the body's] structure, or the majority of [its] count [of bones].

Rashi on Ketubot 28b:6:3.english: That has been trodden - [With] much treading by many feet.

Rashi on Ketubot 28b:6:4.hebrew: טהור - דתלינן לקולא ואמרינן כל העצמות נכתתו לפחות מכשיעור, אלמא חששא דרבנן בעלמא הוא:
Rashi on Ketubot 28b:6:4.english: Is pure - For we rule leniently and say [that] all the bones were crushed to less than the [minimum] measure; thus, it is merely a rabbinic concern.

Rashi on Ketubot 28b:9:1.english: A child is deemed credible - to testify in his adulthood [about] what he saw in his childhood.

Rashi on Ketubot 28b:9:2.english: Impure and pure, does it enter your mind - What impurity and purity is there to say regarding families?

Tosafot on Ketubot 28b:2:1.hebrew: תנן כמאן דאמר אין חולקין לעבד כו' - ואם תאמר: והא לא קאמר רבי יהודה דאין חולקין אלא בתרומה דאורייתא, דמעלין ממנה ליוחסין; אבל מתני', דאוקמינן בתרומה דרבנן, דאין מעלין ממנה ליוחסין — מודה דחולקין לעבד בלא רבו, ואם כן אכתי תקשי: ודלמא עבד כהן הוא? ולאו מלתא היא; דמתניתין איירי שפיר שמעיד שחלק לו תרומה דאורייתא, אלא שאינו נאמן להאכילו אלא בתרומה דרבנן:
Tosafot on Ketubot 28b:2:1.english: "We learned [the Mishnah] according to the one who says: One does not distribute [terumah] to a slave, etc." - And if you say: But Rabbi Yehuda only says that one does not distribute [terumah to a slave without his master] with respect to Biblical terumah, from which we elevate [a person] to [priestly] lineage; however, [regarding] our Mishnah, which we established as referring to rabbinic terumah, from which we do not elevate to [priestly] lineage — he agrees that one distributes [it] to a slave without his master, and if so, it is still difficult: perhaps he is the slave of a priest? [This] is not a [valid] objection, for our Mishnah speaks well [of a case] where he testifies that [the priest] shared Biblical terumah with him, except that he is not believed [on the basis of this testimony] to feed him [anything] other than rabbinic terumah.

Tosafot on Ketubot 28b:4:1.english: "And just as [with regard to] the animals of the righteous" - [This is] explained elsewhere (Gittin 7a).

Tosafot on Ketubot 28b:6:1.hebrew: ושהמקום הזה בית הפרס - ולא יותר, ובא לטהר:
Tosafot on Ketubot 28b:6:1.english: "And that this place is a beit haperas" - [Meaning, this place] and no more, and he comes to declare [the area beyond it] pure.

Tosafot on Ketubot 28b:6:2.hebrew: בית הפרס דרבנן - נראה דאפי' במקום הקבר מקילין כמו בשאר שדה, ואין לומר דמקום הקבר מטמא באהל. ומביא רבינו יצחק ראיה מדתניא בפ"ק דמועד קטן (דף ה:): "מצא שדה מצויינת ואינו יודע מה טיבה, יש בה אילנות — בידוע שנתחרש בה קבר; אין בה אילנות — בידוע שאבד בה קבר". ומאי נפקא מינה, כיון שעתה אינו יודע מקום הקבר, בין נחרש בין אבד? אלא שמע מינה דמקום הקבר טהור כשנחרש. ובית הפרס להכי הוי דרבנן, משום דהוי ספק טומאה ברשות הרבים. אע"ג דבעלמא טיהרו חכמים ספק טומאה ברה"ר — היינו היכא שהטומאה מבוררת ולא נולד הספק אלא באקראי, ופעם אחרת לא יטמא כיון שמקום הטומאה ידוע; אבל הכא, שלעולם השדה בספק, לא רצו לטהר, אע"ג דמדאורייתא טהור:
Tosafot on Ketubot 28b:6:2.english: [The impurity of] a beit haperas is by rabbinic [law] - It appears that even in the place of the grave [itself] we are lenient just like in the rest of the field, and one should not say that the place of the grave imparts impurity by [way of] a tent. And Rabbeinu Yitzchak brings a proof from that which was taught [in a baraita] in the first chapter of Moed Katan (5b): "[If] one found a marked field and does not know what its nature is: [if] there are trees in it, it is known that a grave was plowed over in it; [if] there are no trees in it, it is known that a grave was lost in it." And what is the practical difference, since now he does not know the location of the grave, whether it was plowed over or lost? Rather, learn from this that the place of the grave is pure [from tent impurity] when it has been plowed over. And a beit haperas is [impure] by rabbinic [law] for this reason: because it is a doubt regarding impurity in a public domain. Even though elsewhere the Sages declared a doubt regarding impurity in a public domain pure, that is [only] where the impurity is clearly known and the doubt arose only by chance, and another time one will not become impure since the location of the impurity is known; however, here, where the field is always in doubt, they did not wish to declare [it] pure, even though by Torah law it is pure.

Tosafot on Ketubot 28b:6:3.hebrew: מנפח - בדיעבד, אם עשה כבר טהרות; אבל בדיקה דלכתחלה מפרש במשנה (אהלות פי"ח מ"ד) כיצד בודקין:
Tosafot on Ketubot 28b:6:3.english: [A person] may blow - [This applies] after the fact, if he has already prepared ritually pure [foods]; however, [regarding] an examination at the outset, [the Tanna] explains in the Mishnah (Oholot 18:4) how they examine [a beit haperas].
